author: LT3390

title: Doubted it, shouldn’t have.
body:
Loved the points at the beginning to get be into playing and decorating.
As time went on, seeing the cub evolve as you level up creates more motivation. 
Love the room being decorated as I like.

Didn’t realize how useful this would be. I rely on “cub” heavily and is one of the first things I check into in the morning with my coffee. 

It took a while to get all the chores in there that I needed reminders for and set to the right intervals (which I love how customized it is able to be).  The breakdown into morning / afternoon / evening really helps with organizing the day without seeming to daunting - being able to see the entire day and then into its sections is really helpful for me. The item I check off moving to the bottom and only leaving open tasks is a life changer. 

The mood log, reflection journals, lessons and quizzes, tools and daily quotes are all items I use. Educational, fun and like being able to look back on my mood log. 

I do not have a enough good things to say. 
The more I use it, the more I discover. At this point it is an open app on my phone all the time. A sense of security reducing anxiety being able to check in and know where I’m at for the day and what’s coming.  It’s also great for looking back on days you feel you’ve accomplished nothing - or what your brain thinks is nothing - but I have an entire list checked off in front of me showing me I was productive. 

I could go on and on - this has been a welcome addition to my journey. I’ve been using for a couple months now and am so happy I gave it a shot. I was very uncertain about it, didn’t think it would help or work - this is an instance I will happily say I was wrong. 

If I have one tip for consumers - don’t be afraid to put in a task you think is “so small” it’s ridiculous to list. If it is something you forget or would like to do more consistently, just add it to your routine. I find I’m still adding/changing mine. Those little tasks get done, you feel good about it. I look around and things I used to let slide no longer slide and allows a more peaceful relaxing environment. 

I’ve rambled enough - but you get the point. If you know you know and get the app because I still can’t get over how incredibly useful and beneficial “cub” is to my day to day life (btw - love I got to customize cub and name, etc).

title: Promising, but lots of room to improve
body:
Like a lot of other folks, my primary complaint is that the execution is way too basic. I expected more features, and more of a tamagotchi experience to hold me accountable. I quickly ran out of things to do with the points I accumulated before the free trial ran out. More of a difficulty curve is needed to keep me motivated and feeling like I’m making progress. Now the app is functionally just a checklist with no gamified elements.

I’ll happily pay for the app when I see new features implemented, but right now I don’t think it can justify the cost.
